items.title: Vanishing of the first cohomology of invertible sheaves of degree at least twice the genus minus one on a proper curve
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves H^1(X, L) = 0 for every invertible sheaf of degree at least 2g - 1 on a proper curve over an algebraically closed field, where g = dim_k H^1(X, O_X). The proof takes the invertible module N supplied by the general degree lemma for line bundles, computes its degree as chi(X, N) - chi(X, O_X) = g - 1, and hence finds deg(L tensor N^{-1}) >= g, so that its Euler characteristic is at least one (proof lines 8160-8167). That yields a nonzero global section whose zero scheme is an effective Cartier divisor D of degree deg(L) - (g - 1); the resulting short exact sequence 0 -> N -> L -> i_*(L|_D) -> 0 identifies H^0(X, L) with H^0(D, L|_D), whose dimension is deg(L) - (g - 1), and the result follows from the definition of degree (proof lines 8168-8177). H2: the degree bookkeeping through the auxiliary line bundle and the short exact sequence computation are the substance.
